title: Stopping rules and how a run ended

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A job sets `relative_gap_tolerance=0.005` and nothing else. Its run reports `OPTIMAL` with an incumbent of 51,000 and a best bound of 51,180. A reviewer says the reason must be wrong, because the two bounds differ. Who is right?

options.text: The job, since a gap of about 0.35% is inside its tolerance
options.says: Right: 180 / 51,000 is about 0.35%, within the 0.5% asked for, and a gap stop is reported as OPTIMAL.

options.text: The reviewer, since that reason waits for the two bounds to meet
options.says: MathOpt's gap tolerances let the solver stop with a gap above zero and still report OPTIMAL.

options.text: The reviewer, since a gap above zero is reported as FEASIBLE
options.says: FEASIBLE marks a stop on a limit such as time or nodes; a gap within the tolerance is reported as OPTIMAL.

options.text: Neither, since the reason depends on the time limit in force
options.says: No time limit was set; the reason here comes from the gap tolerance being met.

origin.section: A Gap Stop Ends OPTIMAL; Every Other Limit Ends FEASIBLE or NO_SOLUTION_FOUND

questions.stem: A test solves a MILP with a 5-second time limit and asserts an objective of 7,410. It passes on a laptop and fails on the build server with 7,395. Which change makes the test reliable?

options.text: Raise the limit to 50 seconds, since a longer limit reaches the same plan each run
options.says: A longer time limit still stops wherever a given machine has got to; it promises no particular plan.

options.text: Compare within 1%, since a time limit only rounds the objective it reports
options.says: A time limit stops the search at a different place; the plans differ, not the rounding of one plan.

options.text: Stop on a node limit, since a count of work does not depend on machine speed
options.says: Right: the same model with the same node limit does the same work and, on HiGHS, stops at the same plan.

options.text: Fix the server's clock, since the solver reads the time to pick its branches
options.says: The clock decides only when a time limit fires; the difference comes from how far each machine searched in 5 seconds.

origin.section: Time Limits Are Not Repeatable; Node and Solution Limits Are

questions.stem: A service switches its MILP from HiGHS to CP-SAT through MathOpt and keeps its parameters: `relative_gap_tolerance=0.001` and `node_limit=5000`. What happens on the first solve?

options.text: CP-SAT skips the node limit and stops on the gap tolerance alone
options.says: A solver that cannot honour a parameter refuses the solve; it does not skip the parameter silently.

options.text: The solve raises an exception, since CP-SAT refuses a node limit
options.says: Right: CP-SAT refuses node_limit, and MathOpt raises instead of returning a result.

options.text: CP-SAT reads the node limit as a solution limit and stops early
options.says: No parameter is translated into another; the node limit is refused outright.

options.text: The solve returns NO_SOLUTION_FOUND with the limit set to NODE
options.says: No result is returned at all: the refusal is an exception raised by mathopt.solve.
